webster.text: To make public; to tell or make known something before private or secret; to reveal; to disclose; as, to divulge the secret sentiments of a friend; to divulge the proceedings of the cabinet.

more.text: To declare by a public act; to proclaim.

example.quote: One dissenting person might divulge their misbehavior.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 4, North Carolina Convention, Mr. MACLAINE, July 25, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
